# Make.com Advanced: Routers, Iterators, Aggregators, and Data Stores

## Overview
This is where Make.com's visual model really shines, letting you build logic that would be painful in a linear tool. A Router splits your scenario into multiple branches, and each route can have its own filter so different data follows different paths - premium customers down one branch, everyone else down another - much like Zapier Paths but visually clearer and with more branches. Two of Make.com's most powerful features are the Iterator and the Aggregator, which work as a pair. An Iterator takes an array (say a list of 20 line items in an order) and splits it into 20 separate bundles so you can process each one individually - create a task per item, for instance. An Aggregator does the reverse: it takes many bundles and combines them back into one, so you can, for example, gather all line items and build a single summary text or one array to send onward. Understanding array in, items out, array back together is a concept that trips up beginners but is essential for handling real data. Data Stores are Make.com's built-in mini-database: they let a scenario remember information between runs - storing a list of already-processed IDs so you never handle the same record twice, or keeping a running counter. Variables let you hold and reuse values within a run. Mastering routers, iterators, aggregators, and data stores means you can handle lists, deduplicate, branch, and maintain state - the toolkit for genuinely production-grade no-code automations.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Routers and conditional routes; Filters between modules; Iterators (split an array into items); Aggregators (combine items back together); Data stores and variables for persistence. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
**Practical Task:** Build a Make.com scenario with an iterator that splits an array of items and creates a separate row per item in a sheet, then add an aggregator that also produces a single summary message of all items.
**Mini Project:** Create a scenario that fetches multiple records from an API, uses a router to handle two categories differently, and uses a data store to record which record IDs have already been processed so re-runs skip duplicates.
**Assignment:** Explain the relationship between an iterator and an aggregator with a concrete example, and describe one problem a data store solves that a simple linear workflow cannot.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.

## Assessment
After finishing the work, open the AI Assessment popup to submit your practical results. DeepSeek will evaluate your submission, calculate a dynamic score based on correctness and depth, and add the points to your CalibiAI profile.
